name: Excimer laser for stretch marks

card.summary: A UV laser aimed at repigmenting white stretch marks; the sources show only a tiny early-phase study.
card.aka: 308 nm excimer, UVB laser for striae alba
card.note: Only a 10-person phase 1 registration was found; no published results were reviewed.

quick.overview:
The excimer laser is a 308 nm ultraviolet device used in dermatology, and it has been tried on stretch marks that have faded to white.

The sources reviewed show one small phase 1 trial registration without listed results, so the effect on stretch marks is not established here.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say the ultraviolet light stimulates pigment-producing cells in the pale marks so they darken toward the surrounding skin tone.
quick.risks: The sources reviewed give no safety data for this use. Ultraviolet treatments in general carry considerations that clinicians weigh, but none are documented in the sources used for this article.

lead: The 308 nm excimer laser is an ultraviolet B light device used in dermatology for conditions such as vitiligo, psoriasis and alopecia areata [3][4]. It has also been tried on white (mature) stretch marks, striae alba, whose pale colour comes from loss of pigment. The aim of treatment is to coax pigment cells in the pale streaks to produce melanin so the marks blend closer to the surrounding skin tone, which can make stretch marks on areas such as the torso, hips or thighs less conspicuous.

Stretch marks start out red or purple and later fade to a pale, flattened, atrophic appearance [2]. Wikipedia states that no stretch-mark treatment has been clearly shown to be useful, and that tretinoin and hyaluronic acid are reported to help early marks [2]. For white marks, the most-cited human work on the excimer laser is a 2004 randomized trial of 31 adults at a New York laser centre and a 2010 study of ten Iranian patients, which reached different conclusions about how strong the effect is [5][6].

A 2016 review of laser and light treatments for striae distensae concluded that lasers and light sources can improve the appearance of striae rubra and striae alba [7]. A registered phase 1 study of 308 nm excimer treatment in white striae, begun in 2006 with 10 participants, is also listed [1].

angle.text: The laser is aimed at white stretch marks to bring back colour so they stand out less against nearby skin. Studies describe a visible pigment change during a course of sessions, with maintenance sessions discussed as a way to hold it.

infobox: In-office ultraviolet laser procedure (308 nm xenon chloride)
White (mature) stretch marks, striae alba; hypopigmented scars

paras: Excimer lasers form a short-wavelength ultraviolet beam when an excited xenon and chlorine molecule falls apart; the xenon chloride version emits at 308 nm [3]. In dermatology the beam is aimed at small patches, which lets practitioners treat a lesion while leaving surrounding skin alone. Wikipedia lists vitiligo, psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, alopecia areata and leukoderma among conditions treated with 308 nm excimer devices [3].

For striae alba, the intent is repigmentation: the light acts on the pale marks so they approach the colour of normal skin [5]. In the 2010 Iranian study, the surrounding normal skin was covered with zinc oxide cream during treatment [6].

In a 2004 randomized controlled trial in Archives of Dermatology, Alexiades-Armenakas, Bernstein, Friedman and Geronemus enrolled 31 adults with hypopigmented scars or striae alba. Lesions were randomly assigned to treatment or no treatment and compared with normal skin, with biweekly sessions up to 10. After nine treatments visual pigment correction averaged about 61 percent for scars and 68 percent for striae, and colorimetric values approached those of control skin. The gains declined toward baseline over six months of follow-up, no blistering or dyspigmentation occurred, and the authors concluded that maintenance every one to four months is needed [5].

A 2010 Journal of Dermatological Treatment study by Ostovari and colleagues treated the white lines of striae alba in ten subjects and judged the result by mexameter colorimetry and photographs rated by two dermatologists. The authors reported weak repigmentation, about 80 percent of patients had poor or moderate photographic results, and pigment splaying was a main side effect [6].

A 2016 comprehensive review of laser and light treatments for striae distensae covered lasers for both red and white stretch marks [7]. A phase 1 study (NCT00361361) on 308 nm excimer laser in white striae began in July 2006 with 10 participants and is listed as completed, with no results posted in the registry record [1].
The 2004 trial reported no blistering or dyspigmentation [5]. The 2010 study named pigment splaying, in which colour spreads beyond the treated line, as a major side effect [6].

Wikipedia says no treatment is clearly established for stretch marks, while topical tretinoin 0.1 percent has been reported effective on early stretch marks in several studies, hyaluronic acid has been reported to improve appearance, and micrografting is experimental [2]. Excimer treatment targets the later, pale stage, which these topical approaches address less.
The procedure is mentioned in body-skin and hardmaxxing discussions as an option for stretch marks that have already turned white. No forum threads specific to it were identified.

timeline.event: Randomized trial of 308 nm excimer laser for hypopigmented scars and striae alba, 31 adults, published in Archives of Dermatology [5].
